decision: Rewrote scripts/night/N6/privacy_scan.py. It now scans site/, deliverable/ and build/out/ by default (--paths for other scopes), and catches house numbers of any length (1-5 digits) in any case, addresses with no street type after a direction, two-number labels ('N & M'), ranges, and 'N block of' with N not a multiple of 100. A hundred number counts as a house number unless the text says 'block of'. The only exemption is house number 1234 with EXAMPLE in the same address. Each hit is checked against the city's own address lists (MSD service addresses plus 311 addresses, 256,601 pairs): real hits always fail the gate. Precision rules decide what counts as an address or a coordinate, never which addresses may pass: a street needs a word before its type; a route number (Interstate, I-, Hwy, Route, US, MO) is not a house number; a coordinate is a lat/lon or Web Mercator pair (a lone 38.6 days is not); a decimal fraction or an app id is not a parcel id. Address-shaped hits that match no city address and whose 'street' contains a function word or month go to a 'review' list that is printed but does not fail the gate.
why: N8 re-check: the gate skipped house numbers under 10 and all lower-case addresses, scanned site/ only, had a '1234' allowlist and never matched the 'N & M' pattern that leaked. Run on the 01:26 snapshot, the new scan finds the two risks.md labels (both real addresses) and 13 'N00 block of NN STREET' rows (a range's second number kept) in each Monday list file, a leak N8 did not report. After the rebuild: 0 findings, 47 review hits, all prose ('Q2 2026 residential and alley', 'wards 6-14 for Street Department', '(31 Oct row)').
alternative_rejected: Fail the gate on every address-shaped hit including prose (a gate that is always red gets ignored); keep the old allowlist of years and lower case (missed real addresses numbered 1900-2099 and lower-case text).
